# Engagement Standard Operating Procedure
This procedure applies to Security and command staff whenever they engage an antagonist. The aim is a round worth playing for everyone in it, not the fastest possible kill.
## Engage in Numbers
Do not rush an antagonist alone. A lone officer forces a kill-or-be-killed exchange and ends the encounter before a word is spoken.
Call it in, wait for backup, and move as a group. Numbers even the odds, and even odds are what make an arrest possible instead of a body.
## No Valid Hunting
Do not go hunting the moment you suspect somebody. Confirm it, report it, and plan the approach.
Lethal force on sight is a last resort under [textlink="Security SOP" link="GuideSecuritySOP"], never an opening move. An arrest and an interrogation give the shift somewhere to go; a corpse in a hallway does not.
## Patience Over Speed
Contain and cordon rather than charging a hardened target. Cut off escape, hold the line, and talk where it is safe to do so.
Time spent waiting for a second officer is almost always cheaper than time spent in cryo.
## Command Is Held To This Too
Command staff [bold]shall not[/bold] lead a charge, and [bold]shall not[/bold] order one. Directing the crew to swarm a suspect is the same failure as doing it yourself, with more bodies.
[italic]Antagonists are bound by the mirror of this procedure. See [textlink="Antagonist SOP" link="GuideAntagonistSOP"].[/italic]
